prompt: 我在观察一个现象：我们团队的 code review 文化虽然流程上很完整（每个 PR 都要求至少两个 reviewer 签字，checklist 很详尽，review 平均耗时 2 天），但实际效果在慢慢退化。评审越来越流程化、仪式化，深度问题（架构、设计、潜在bug）越来越少被指出，大家更倾向于只看代码风格和边界条件。在我写改进提案之前，帮我想清楚：这里真正发生了什么？

assertions.text: Treats the question as DIAGNOSTIC (what is happening and why) rather than PRESCRIPTIVE (how to fix). Does not jump to '5 tips to improve code reviews'.

Elevates to abstract structural framing (e.g. Goodhart's law, ritualization under incentive misalignment, process-as-substitute-for-judgment, Chesterton's fence in reverse) rather than listing observable symptoms.
Offers at least one cross-domain analogue (academic peer review degradation / medical chart rounds / org-level bureaucratization / bureaucratic theater / scientific replication crisis / etc.).
Names at least one fundamental tension AS A SHAPE — e.g. '流程合规 ↔ 深度判断', '心理安全 ↔ 尖锐批评', 'process legibility ↔ judgment-based quality' — without prematurely resolving.
Includes at least three structurally different perspectives (e.g. reviewer / reviewee / manager; or insider / outsider / time-one-year-later).
Names the underlying pattern — e.g. '仪式化替代了判断', 'ritualization-under-incentive-misalignment', 'compliance-theater supplanting craftsmanship', or an invented-if-needed concrete name.
Does NOT immediately list action items / fixes. The user explicitly said 'before I write a proposal' — the output stays diagnostic.
Does NOT announce the scaffold (no 'Using awaken skill', no Q1/Q2/Q3 markers). Response is in Chinese (matching the user's language).

Surfaces at least one non-obvious contributing cause the user may not have considered (e.g. team size or composition shift, incentive structure around shipping, loss of senior reviewers, load distribution, asynchronous review fatigue).
